title: Completeness of the numerical encoding
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $A$ be a Boolean answer table. Suppose that for every query and every $t,a<2^W$, $A$ agrees with the machine's tabulated answer at time $t$ and index $a$. Let $x_b$ be a Boolean sequence that agrees with $x$ at every index below $|x|$, and assume $|x|+2<2^W$. If the machine's configuration after $2^W-1$ steps has halted and its output register records exactly the single bit $1$, then every local check passes under the numerical valuation determined by $A,W,|x|,t,a,j,x_b(j)$, for all $t,a<2^W$, all $j\le |x|+1$, and every check type.
